Follow your **Octopus Energy France** contract (electricity and gas, formerly
Plüm Énergie) in Gladys: the consumption your Linky or Gazpar meter reports,
its cost, your account balance, the next payment, and above all the
**off-peak hours** (heures creuses) of your contract, to the minute, to start
the water heater or the car charge at the right time.

Electricity also feeds the Gladys 5.2 **energy tracking**, day by day, on the
date it was really consumed, even though Enedis sends the readings a day or
two late.

> Not affiliated with Octopus Energy. **Developed without the hardware:
> feedback welcome** — developed without an Octopus Energy account: your
> feedback is welcome (GitHub issues or the Gladys forum). The exchanges with
> Octopus follow the open-source Home Assistant integration
> ha-octopus-french, but could not be tried with a real account.

## Overview

- One Gladys device per **supply point**: an electricity meter (the PRM
  number of your Linky) and a gas meter (the PCE number of your Gazpar), when
  your contract has both.
- **Electricity**: the dated consumption goes to the Gladys energy tracking;
  plus the consumption and cost of the last day read and of the month, the
  account balance, the next payment, the name of the offer, and the current
  tariff period (peak or off-peak hours) with its price.
- **Gas**: the same summaries in kWh and euros, the balance and the next
  payment.
- A dashboard widget, three scene triggers and a scene action.
- The account is read every 3 hours. The off-peak hours are followed to the
  minute, without connecting to Octopus.

## Requirements

- Gladys **5.2.0** or later (import of a consumption dated in the past).
- An electricity or gas contract with **Octopus Energy France** and access to
  your customer area (e-mail address and password). Octopus customers in the
  United Kingdom or another country are not concerned: their platform is a
  different one.
- A smart meter (Linky, Gazpar) for the daily consumption. Without one, only
  the balance, the payment and the contract are shown.
- Internet access for your Gladys: the integration talks to the Octopus
  Energy France API (`api.oefr-kraken.energy`).

## Configuration

Install the integration from **Integrations → Install from GitHub** (or from
the store), then fill in:

| Field                    | What to enter                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| E-mail address           | The sign-in address of your Octopus Energy customer area                             |
| Password                 | The password of that customer area                                                   |
| History to import        | Electricity days sent to the energy tracking on the first reading (7 days to 1 year) |
| Language of device names | Language of the feature names (French by default), set when you add a meter          |

Save: the integration signs in, reads the account and offers your meters in
the **Discovery** tab. Add them; their values arrive at once.

The **Sign in and refresh now** button reads the account again without
waiting for the 3-hour cycle (once every quarter of an hour at most).

When Octopus refuses the address or the password, the integration stops and
does not try again until you fix the configuration: too many failures could
lock your account.

## Devices

Each meter is a device named after its energy and the last four digits of
its number, for example "Octopus Electricity …0123".

### Electricity meter

| Feature                        | Unit   | What it is                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Daily consumption              | kWh    | The consumption of each day, dated, for the Gladys energy tracking                                 |
| Last day consumption           | kWh    | The last complete day read by Enedis (often the day before yesterday)                              |
| Last day cost                  | €      | Its cost incl. taxes as computed by Octopus, standing charge excluded                              |
| Month consumption              | kWh    | The month of the last reading, up to that day                                                      |
| Month cost                     | €      | Its cost incl. taxes without standing charge, only when every day of it has a cost                 |
| Account balance                | €      | The balance of your electricity account at Octopus: positive in your favour, negative when you owe |
| Next payment                   | €      | The amount of the next planned direct debit                                                        |
| Next payment date              | text   | Its date                                                                                           |
| Offer                          | text   | The name of your offer                                                                             |
| Off-peak hours now             | yes/no | 1 during the off-peak hours of your contract, 0 otherwise                                          |
| Tariff period                  | text   | "Off-peak hours", "Peak hours" or "Base rate"                                                      |
| Current price per kWh          | €      | The price per kWh incl. taxes of the current period                                                |
| Off-peak hours of the contract | text   | The off-peak ranges, for example "22:00–06:00"                                                     |

### Gas meter

The same summaries, without the daily consumption nor the off-peak hours:
**Last day consumption**, **Last day cost**, **Month consumption**, **Month
cost** (in kWh, as on your bills), **Account balance**, **Next payment**,
**Next payment date** and **Offer**. Octopus gives no cost with the gas
readings, so it is computed at the price per kWh incl. taxes of your
contract, standing charge excluded. A Gazpar that only sends a monthly
reading shows the month only.

## Energy tracking

Enedis sends the Linky readings to Octopus a day or two late. Gladys 5.2 can
import a consumption dated in the past: the integration sends each day on its
real date, through the dedicated core endpoint, and sends the last three days
again at every reading (Enedis sometimes corrects its recent readings;
Gladys writes only what changed). The Gladys energy charts and the cost
computed from your contract are therefore right despite the delay.

No cumulative index is published, on purpose: Gladys would turn an index
received a day late into a single half hour of consumption.

For Gladys to compute the costs, choose the **Daily consumption** feature of
your electricity meter as the main meter in the energy settings and create
your contract there. The **Last day cost** and **Month cost** features come
from Octopus and do not depend on that contract.

Gas is not sent to the energy tracking: Gladys 5.2 prices electricity only,
and a gas consumption would be added to the electricity one.

## Off-peak hours and tariff period

The integration reads the off-peak hours of your contract, from the most
precise source to the least precise:

1. the time slots of the off-peak rate of your Octopus contract;
2. the supplier calendar of your meter;
3. the off-peak hours the Linky announces ("HC (22H00-6H00)").

Every minute, without connecting to Octopus, it works out the current
period, in French legal time (clock changes included), publishes **Off-peak
hours now**, **Tariff period** and **Current price per kWh**, and fires the
scenes when the period changes.

- **Base** offer: a single period, all day.
- **Peak / off-peak** offer: the period and its price.
- **Two-season** offer (summer and winter peak and off-peak hours): the
  ranges and the price of the current season.
- **Tempo**-like offer: the period is given, but not the price, which
  depends on the colour of the day that Octopus does not announce in the
  account.

## Dashboard widget

**Octopus Energy** shows, for one meter (the first electricity meter when you
choose none): the date of the last reading, the consumption of that day and
of the month, their cost, the last 14 days as bars, the current tariff period
and until when, the price per kWh, the account balance and the next payment.
It updates at every reading and at every change of period. When the
configuration is missing or the password is refused, the widget says so.

## Scene triggers and action

- **Off-peak hours start** (trigger): fires on the minute the off-peak hours
  of your contract start. Optionally choose the meter. Variables: the end of
  the off-peak hours (`until`, HH:MM) and the off-peak price (`price`,
  €/kWh).
- **Off-peak hours end** (trigger): fires on the minute they end and the peak
  hours begin. Variables: the time of the next off-peak hours (`until`) and
  the peak price (`price`).
- **New day of readings** (trigger): Octopus received a new complete day from
  the Linky or the Gazpar, often a day or two late. Optionally filter on the
  meter or the energy. Variables: the day (`date`, YYYY-MM-DD), its
  consumption (`consumption`, kWh) and its cost (`cost`), the consumption and
  cost of the month (`month_consumption`, `month_cost`), the energy
  (`energy`: `electricity` or `gas`). Fired once per new day; the first
  reading after the installation only sets the starting point.
- **Read an Octopus meter summary** (action): gives the last day read, its
  consumption and cost, the consumption and cost of the month, the balance,
  the next payment and its date, the tariff period (`base`, `peak` or
  `off_peak`) and the current price, for the next actions of the scene. An
  unknown figure stays empty.

Why triggers on top of **Off-peak hours now**? The state is published again
regularly (every 6 hours) so that Gladys does not consider it stale: a scene
"when the state is 1" could start again. The triggers fire only once, when
the period changes, and never at a restart. Use the state as a **condition**
("only during off-peak hours") and the triggers to **start** a scene.

## Scene examples

- **Water heater on off-peak hours**: trigger _Off-peak hours start_ → turn
  the water heater plug on; trigger _Off-peak hours end_ → turn it off.
- **Car charge**: trigger _Off-peak hours start_ → turn the charging point on,
  send "Charge started until \{\{triggerEvent.data.until\}\}".
- **Delayed washing machine**: when the "start later" button is pressed,
  condition **Off-peak hours now** = 1 → start at once, otherwise wait for
  the trigger.
- **Daily report**: trigger _New day of readings_ (energy: electricity) →
  message "\{\{triggerEvent.data.date\}\}: \{\{triggerEvent.data.consumption\}\} kWh,
  \{\{triggerEvent.data.cost\}\} €. Month: \{\{triggerEvent.data.month_cost\}\} €."
- **Weekly report**: a scene scheduled on Sundays → _Read an Octopus meter
  summary_ → message with the month cost and the balance.

## Refresh and quotas

- One reading of the account every 3 hours; a new try after an hour when
  Octopus does not answer or asks to slow down (API request limit, error
  KT-CT-1199).
- A reading costs about ten requests: the sign-in (the access token lasts an
  hour, the refresh token a week, without sending the password again), the
  list of accounts, the account, and the readings of each meter. The first
  reading imports the chosen history: four more requests for a year. The
  Home Assistant integration reads every hour: this is three times less.
- The off-peak hours are computed in Gladys, without a request.
- The integration polls itself: it does not depend on the Gladys polling.
- The terms of use of Octopus Energy apply to your account: this integration
  only reads your own data, read-only.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Octopus Energy refused the e-mail address or the password"**: check them
  by signing in to your Octopus customer area, then fix the configuration
  (the integration then tries again at once).
- **"Octopus Energy cannot be reached"**: the API did not answer; a new try
  within the hour. If it lasts, Octopus may have changed its API: open a
  GitHub issue with the logs.
- **No meter offered**: the account has no active supply point yet (a
  terminated meter is not offered).
- **The last day is the day before yesterday**: normal, Enedis and GRDF send
  the readings late.
- **No daily consumption**: your meter may not be a smart one, or you did not
  allow the collection of your consumption data in your customer area.
- **No tariff period**: Octopus gave neither the off-peak ranges of the
  contract nor those of the meter. Report it with the name of your offer.
- **Logs**: set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see every reading. The logs never show
  the e-mail address, the password nor the tokens.

## Limitations

- **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome** — developed without
  an Octopus account. The requests follow those of the Home Assistant
  integration ha-octopus-french, not a real try: the first real uses may
  reveal differences.
- The readings are a day or two late: no instant power, no "today". For real
  time, use a teleinformation module on your Linky.
- The energy tracking receives days, not half hours: a peak / off-peak
  contract created in Gladys cannot split a day between its two prices. The
  Octopus cost features do.
- Gas is outside the energy tracking.
- Tempo offers: no current price, nor colour of the day. Managed offers
  (Octopus Intelligent, vehicle charging) are not supported.
- The gas cost is estimated at the price per kWh of your contract; the costs
  never include the standing charge.
- One sign-in per integration; every account and meter of that sign-in is
  offered.
- No command: the integration controls nothing at Octopus.

## Privacy and data

The e-mail address and the password stay in the Gladys configuration. The
`/data/octopus-state.json` file keeps the Octopus refresh token (so the
password is not sent at every reading) and, for each meter, how far the
energy tracking was fed. Only the integration can read it. Nothing is sent
anywhere but to the Octopus Energy France API and to your Gladys.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Octopus Energy France asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Octopus Energy customer area | `section` | No | Sign in with the e-mail address and password of your Octopus Energy France customer area. Linky and Gazpar readings arrive a day or two late and are read every 3 hours. Not affiliated with Octopus Energy. |
| E-mail address | `string` | Yes |  |
| Password | `secret` | Yes |  |
| History to import | `select` | No | Electricity days sent to the Gladys energy tracking on the first reading. |
| Language of device names | `select` | No | Names are set when you add a meter to Gladys. |

## How to install Octopus Energy France in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Octopus Energy France appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-octopus-fr:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-octopus-fr](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-octopus-fr).

Octopus Energy France requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
